entries.question: [R-LENS-03]'s LENS_REGISTRY is a CLOSED enumeration keyed on the lessons register's own class list, and a study must map into one of its thirteen rows to publish a lens record. SAVOLA — food manufacturing, grocery retail and a listed quick-service stake — maps to none of them, and BOTH available routes are barred by rules this house already holds. Adding a row is barred because the rule says in terms that a class is added when a DIFFERENT LENS carries the weight and never merely when the industry differs, and a grocer's lens set is identical to three rows already there (primary cash flow; cross-checks own-history EV/EBITDA, a relative multiple and book). Mapping it to one of those rows is barred because a name resolving to the wrong subject is worse than an absence — calling a supermarket group a telecom operator would put that label in the study's own record. So SAVOLA cannot retire its typed 45/25/15/15 blend under [R-LENS-03] without one of the two being decided.

routes.route: research_protocol.LENS_REGISTRY and lessons_register.CLASSES, read live and compared — the registry asserts on the class list at import, so the two cannot be changed independently
routes.outcome: 13 classes; three rows (telecom operator, airline, pharmaceutical manufacturer) carry an IDENTICAL lens set. The duplication is the evidence: the registry keys on an industry NAME while the thing it stores is a lens SET.

routes.route: every study directory's committed lens_record, for a precedent mapping an operating company to a row named for another industry
routes.outcome: none — every conforming study's declared class matches its actual industry, so there is no house precedent for borrowing a row.

routes.route: the standing protocol and the digest, for what [R-LENS-03] says about a class that fits nothing
routes.outcome: The exemplar clause covers the analogous case for REPORTS ('adapt the nearest pattern's lens inside the skeleton and say which and why') and the registry clause does not carry the equivalent for CLASSES. The gap is in the rule, not in the study.

routes.route: research_protocol.LENS_REGISTRY read against a SECOND name that meets the same wall — EMPOWER, a regulated district-cooling utility on the DFM
routes.outcome: no row either, and the wall is the same one: a chilled-water network's lens set is a cash-flow primary cross-checked on its own EV/EBITDA history, a relative multiple and book — identical to the three duplicate rows already there — so adding a class would again be adding it for an INDUSTRY difference, which the rule forbids in terms. TWO INDEPENDENT NAMES IN ONE WEEK IS THE SECOND OBSERVATION [R-LESSON-01] asks for before widening a finding.

routes.route: every study UNREADABLE to the valuation-gap gate, read to the leaf that carries its arithmetic — checking whether this wall is one name's problem or the group's
routes.outcome: IT IS THE GROUP'S, and the group is larger than anyone had counted. All SEVEN studies invisible to [R-GAP-01] are invisible for this exact reason: each publishes a multi-lens combination [R-LENS-03] retired and therefore no single central. ADNOCDIST 40/25/20/15 twice (lenses.items_A), ADNOCDRILL 25/25/20/15/15 (fair_value.weights), ELEC 40/20/20/20 (compute.py:505, and its delivered document prints the words), GBCO 40/15/20/25 (compute.py:258-260), STC 35/25/20/20 (stc_compute.py:277), AMR 50/20/20/10 (lenses.weights), BOROUGE the MEDIAN of nine readings across two beta framings and two scenarios (compute.py:722). AND FOUR OF THE SEVEN MEET THE SAME WALL AS SAVOLA AND EMPOWER: fuel retail, restaurants, offshore drilling and cable manufacturing are in no row of the registry, and none of them is a DIFFERENT LENS — every one is a cash-flow primary with a relative multiple and book beside it. So the count of names this gap blocks is now NINE, not two, and eight of them cannot publish a readable answer until it is settled.

routes.route: GBCO's own delivered document and committed numbers, opened rather than inferred — the one name of the nine the count had placed on the OTHER side
routes.outcome: IT IS THE FIFTH INSTANCE, NOT ONE OF THE THREE THAT CAN PROCEED, and it is the SHARPEST case for the default fix rather than a complication of it. The 5-Sep count above put GBCO among the three studies with a registered class; its own masthead and section 1.1 say otherwise in terms — 'we value GB Corp as an operating company with a captive finance arm and split the legs', primary lens 'split-the-legs sum-of-the-parts (operating company + captive lender)'. THERE IS NO ROW FOR THAT. What makes it the sharpest case is what happens next: the registry's holding-company row stores EXACTLY the lens set GBCO needs — an SOTP primary with a relative multiple and book beside it — so the registry already contains the right answer and refuses it on the ROW'S NAME ALONE. GB Corp is not a holding company by the rule's own test (a holdco IS its stakes; this is an auto assembler-distributor with a captive lender and one large associate), and filing it as one would put that label in its committed record, which is the 'wrong subject is worse than an absence' bar. Under the default fix — rows named for their lens sets — GBCO maps with nobody inventing a fit, exactly as SAVOLA does. So the affected count is FIVE of the seven unreadable studies and NINE names in total, and the only one of the seven that can take the lever today is STC (telecom operator, a row that exists).

routes.route: the four eight-heading gap reviews written on 5 September, read for what each one names as its LARGEST priced correction
routes.outcome:
ALL FOUR NAME THE SAME ONE, AND ALL FOUR ARE BLOCKED BY THIS ESCALATION. Until tonight the cost of this delay was measured in readability — seven studies the valuation-gap gate could say nothing about. Four of those are now readable and audited, and every one of the four reviews reaches the same verdict: the gap is OURS and the single largest correction is retiring the typed multi-lens blend under [R-LENS-03]. AMR: the class primary alone is 2.2333 against a published 2.1455, closing 36% of a -10.2% gap and clearing the publication block on its own. ADNOCDRILL: the two cash-flow framings STRADDLE the price and their midpoint lands 0.04% from it, so three-quarters of a -15.2% gap is the blend and nothing else — worth +0.88 to +1.29 a share. ADNOCDIST: the blend is DAMPING a premium, and the primary alone is +19.0% / +26.9% rather than +9.7% / +14.0%, which is the correction running the OTHER way and is worth +0.37 / +0.52. ELEC: two of its four lenses are pinned at floors carrying 60% of the weight, so the blend is not merely a blend, it is what makes a clamped model publishable at all.
NONE OF THE FOUR CAN TAKE IT. Restaurants, offshore drilling, fuel retail and cable manufacturing are in no row of the registry, and not one of them needs a LENS the registry lacks — every one is a cash-flow primary with a relative multiple and book beside it, exactly as the default fix describes. So the delay now blocks the largest identified correction on four audited studies simultaneously, and on two of them it blocks a correction that would move the answer AWAY from the price, which is the shape that proves the answer is not being chosen for where it lands.

entries.why_only_the_principal: Both routes require changing a standing rule rather than applying one: either [R-LENS-03]'s bar on adding a class for an industry difference, or the taxonomy the lessons register and the lens registry share. A rule amendment is the principal's, and taking it inside a study rebuild is exactly the per-name exception this house forbids everywhere else.
entries.done_meanwhile: SAVOLA's two terminal levers were taken in full — growth stored as a real rate on the house Saudi path, and the terminal rebuilt through the sanctioned module on an asset life DERIVED by identity from note 6's own cost and depreciation columns. The blend is left standing and SAVOLA stays on the lens ratchet, where it already sat legitimately. The cost of leaving it is measured and stated rather than implied: the blend publishes 27.28 against a cash-flow lens of 25.02, so retiring it would move the central 8.3% DOWN and the gap against the latest price from -10.0% to -17.4%. EMPOWER meets the identical wall and is left standing for the identical reason: its terminal was rebuilt in full through the sanctioned module on a derived 28.10-year life, and its typed 50/20/15/15 blend stays, with the cost measured rather than implied — the blend publishes 1.8523 against a cash-flow lens of 2.1335, so retiring it would move the central 15.2% UP and the gap against the latest 1.57 from +18.0% to +35.9%. THE TWO NAMES MOVE IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, which is the strongest evidence available that this is a taxonomy question and not a valuation one: on SAVOLA the blend flatters and on EMPOWER it discounts, so no answer to it can be chosen for the number it produces.
entries.default_if_no_answer: RENAME THE REGISTRY'S ROWS FOR THEIR LENS SETS RATHER THAN FOR INDUSTRIES, and merge the three duplicates into one row — an operating company valued on its own cash flows and cross-checked on its own EV/EBITDA history, a relative multiple and book. That is not adding a class for an industry: it is naming the registry for the thing it actually stores, which makes the closed enumeration closable. SAVOLA then maps to it without anybody inventing a fit.
entries.note: The gap is worth naming beyond this one name: the registry is keyed on an industry NAME and stores a lens SET, and three of its thirteen rows already store the same set. A taxonomy that must grow per industry, under a rule that forbids growing per industry, has no state in which a new operating company can be added — which is a property of the design rather than of any study that meets it. EMPOWER adds one thing the first instance could not show: its blend carries a NORMALISED EARNINGS lens at 15%, and normalised earnings appears in no row of the registry at all. So even under the default fix — rename the rows for their lens sets and merge the duplicates — that lens still has to go, which is the rule working as intended rather than a further gap in it. [5-Sep-2026] The evidence has widened from two names to nine and the shape has not changed, which is what makes the default fix look right rather than expedient: not one of the seven added today needs a lens the registry lacks — they need a ROW WHOSE NAME IS NOT AN INDUSTRY. And the cost of the delay is now measurable in a second currency: these seven are exactly the studies the valuation-gap gate can say nothing about, so a taxonomy question is holding a PUBLICATION gate blind over a third of the book. [5-Sep-2026, second reading] GBCO was counted on the wrong side of this wall for a day and the correction matters twice over. It raises the blocked count from four of the seven to five, and it supplies the case that settles the DESIGN question rather than adding another instance of it: every earlier name needed a row whose NAME is not an industry while the LENS SET was already there three times over; GBCO needs a row whose name is not an industry while the lens set is there ONCE, under a name that is a real and different subject. A taxonomy keyed on industry cannot express 'an operating company valued on its parts' without either inventing a class for every industry that is one, or calling an auto assembler a holding company. THE OBSERVATION THAT WAS MISSED IS ALSO WORTH KEEPING: this session asserted GBCO could proceed and wrote it into the programme state before opening GBCO's own document, which is L-334 and L-335 for the sixth time in one session.

entries.question: The two figures in note (4/11) on page 61 of EGCH_FY2019-20_Annual.pdf: the amount DRAWN in US dollars and the amount DRAWN in Egyptian pounds on the natural-gas conversion facility. They fix the currency split of EGCH's borrowings, which its walk-forward currently treats as 100% dollar — a 'stated simplification' its own module flags and the filings refute.

routes.route: pdftotext over all ten held filings
routes.outcome: the text layer is a broken font map on Arabic scans; an English keyword search returned nothing, which read exactly like an absence and was not one

routes.route: pdftoppm at 200 dpi + tesseract -l ara over every page of every filing
routes.outcome: died on a 180s per-page timeout at page 2 of the oldest filing — a PROBE FAILURE, re-run rather than believed

routes.route: re-pointed sweep: back 45% of each filing, 420s per page, timeouts named
routes.outcome: COMPLETED, zero pages timed out, all ten filings read. Found the note in four filings and the DRAWN-amounts sentence in FY2019-20 page 61

routes.route: pdftoppm at 450 and 500 dpi + tesseract -l ara on the located page
routes.outcome: prose resolves; the two digit strings do not

routes.route: magnified crop (x1.6, x3), binarised, tesseract psm 6/7/11/13 with a digit-only whitelist
routes.outcome: four mutually inconsistent digit strings across four modes; none footable

entries.why_only_the_principal: Not a judgement and not an instruction — a READING. The figures are on a page held in this repository and every extraction route available here has been run and failed on Arabic-Indic digits in a low-quality scan. A person opening EGCH_FY2019-20_Annual.pdf at page 61 can read them in seconds. Nothing else in the room can.
entries.done_meanwhile: The finding that does not need the digits was established and committed: four filings state the facility in BOTH currencies (~117m USD and 1.887bn EGP from six named Egyptian banks, interest and instalments in both), so the 100%-dollar treatment is refuted on four filings rather than one. The FX line was also bounded without any currency assumption — the realised result sits outside every net-dollar-position construction in 9 of 12 years — so the SIGN is wrong, not the weighting, and that conclusion stands whatever the split turns out to be.
entries.default_if_no_answer: Leave EGCH's FX driver exactly as it is and leave the run on the frozen-escalator ratchet. Do NOT estimate a share: a dollar weight invented to make the line behave is the free parameter the promotion rule forbids, and the refutation already stands without it. Record the split as sourced-but-unread in the run's own register so the next reader finds the page reference rather than the question.
entries.note: Registered under [R-IND-01] rather than asked in a message. Twice tonight a 'cannot be obtained' on this same line turned out to be wrong on closer looking — the currency note itself, then the balance split — and both times the FIRST PROBE was what failed while its failure read like an absence. That is why five routes are listed with outcomes and why the sweep that succeeded is marked as a re-run.
